content: {"summary":"To tell a retry storm from a plain slow dependency during the 26 May 2026 checkout 504s, look at the order of symptoms and the request‑ratio pattern. A retry storm shows latency that keeps climbing after the initial cause disappears, a surge of bottom‑layer errors (CPX‑W429) that appear after edge 504s, and many more calls to the processor than to the upstream services. A plain slow dependency shows only increased latency without the disproportionate bottom‑heavy traffic and without later 429 spikes. The May incident was caused by the processor throttling (CPX‑W429) combined with stacked retries that amplified traffic to nine attempts per checkout.","likely_cause":"Retry storm caused by processor rate‑limit (CPX‑W429) and stacked retries across orders‑api, payments‑api, and the proxy","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A retry storm manifests as latency that keeps climbing after the initial cause is gone and more requests at the bottom than at the top.","evidence_ids":["RB-016#1"],"quote":"latency that keeps climbing after the cause is gone, plus more requests at the bottom than at the top."},{"text":"If edge 504s started first and the 429s only came later, the 429s are likely caused by our own retry traffic, indicating a retry storm.","evidence_ids":["RB-016#3"],"quote":"If edge `504`s started first and the 429s only came later, our own retry traffic probably caused the 429s."},{"text":"When CPX‑W429 errors lead, the processor is pushing back and our retries amplify the problem.","evidence_ids":["RB-016#3"],"quote":"If `CPX-W429` leads, the processor is pushing back and our retries are making it worse."},{"text":"The checkout path can multiply a single request into up to nine attempts against the processor, which can turn a slow processor into a retry storm.","evidence_ids":["RB-016#0"],"quote":"That's up to nine attempts against the processor for one button press."}],"next_checks":["Monitor the timestamps of edge 504s versus CPX‑W429 spikes to see which appears first","Compare per‑hop request counts (edge → orders → payments → proxy) for a bottom‑heavy ratio","Track latency trends after the edge stops returning 504s to see if it continues climbing","Temporarily set CPX_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 in payments‑api and observe whether 504s and 429s drop quickly"]}
